channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [7] Magnetic control of an exciton–polariton condensate in a van der Waals magnet
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Florian Dirnberger, Rupert Huber

Authors: Heng Zhang, Niloufar Nilforoushan, Christian Weidgans, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Exciton-polariton dynamics in a van der Waals magnet relevant to quantum materials experiments.

Tags: #vanderWaals #magnetism #exciton-polariton

Abstract: Magnetically tunable exciton–polariton condensation is demonstrated in CrSBr, a van der Waals magnet, using microwires embedded in an optical cavity under photoexcitation. The observation may enable ultrafast control of condensate emission through coupling to coherent magnons.

item.title: [6] Ultrafast anisotropic valleytronics in SnSe
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Fabio Caruso, Samuel Beaulieu

Authors: Yiming Pan, Sotirios Fragkos, Dominique Descamps, Stéphane Petit, Fabio Caruso, Samuel Beaulieu

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Anisotropic valley dynamics in a 2D material, adjacent to electronic structure interests.

Tags: #material #valleytronics #ultrafast

Abstract: Polarization-selective excitation in SnSe reveals anisotropic valley dynamics with distinct channels: one channel with near-unity valley polarization and one channel that rapidly depolarizes through electron–phonon-mediated intervalley scattering.

item.title: [8] Single-stripe magnetic order and bilayer spin dynamics in single-crystalline La3Ni2O7
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Qisi Wang, Jun Zhao

Authors: Lixing Chen, Enkang Zhang, Yiqing Hao, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important neutron scattering study on the magnetic order of a new nickelate superconductor.

Tags: #nickelate #superconductivity #neutronscattering

Abstract: Momentum-resolved neutron scattering of a mosaic of single crystals of La3Ni2O7, a parent compound of nickelate superconductors, is reported. The magnetic behaviour of these nickelate crystals is distinct from that of cuprates and furthers our understanding of the origin of superconductivity in this class of materials.

item.title: [7] Polarization vortices in a ferromagnetic metal via twistronics
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Jordi Arbiol, Gustau Catalan

Authors: Yingzhuo Lun, Xinxin Hu, Qi Ren, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Topological states in twisted membranes of the correlated metal SrRuO3.

Tags: #twistronics #topological #ferromagnet

Abstract: Polar topological states are realized in stacked and twisted 10-nm-thick metallic ferromagnetic SrRuO3 membranes, and their emergence is attributed to flexoelectric effects arising from shear strain gradients.
